name: HSV (HSB)
description: Hue-Saturation-Value (also called HSB: Hue-Saturation-Brightness). A cylindrical remapping of sRGB. Similar to HSL but with a different model: V=1 always gives the most saturated color at that hue, which maps more intuitively to artist 'color pickers'.

S.name: Saturation
S.notes: 0 = achromatic (gray), 1 = fully saturated. Unlike HSL, saturation meaning is consistent at all values of V.

V.name: Value (Brightness)
V.notes: 0 = black, 1 = maximum brightness for that hue. At V=1, S=1 you get the pure hue.

vs_hsl.key_difference: In HSL, L=0.5 gives pure hue. In HSV, V=1 gives pure hue. HSV matches the mental model of 'adding black' (decrease V) or 'adding white' (decrease S).

HSV_to_HSL: S_hsl = 0 if L=0 or L=1, else (V-L)/min(L, 1-L)

use_cases: Color pickers in creative applications (Photoshop, Figma, etc.)
When you want saturation to mean the same thing regardless of brightness

harmony_algebra.note: H channel is identical to HSL — all harmony angle operations apply equally. Convert to HSL for harmony math, then back to HSV for display if needed.

art_notes: HSV is what most color pickers use under the hood. The square/rectangle color picker grid is HSV space — one axis is S, the other is V, with H set by the hue slider. Useful to understand when building your own color tools.
